_doc: Ordered rules, first match wins. See scripts/command-center/parts-check.mjs. "broad" = catch-all not counted for multi-match warnings; "doubtful" = placement needs owner review. A part has ONE home (system, layer) and may list "also": other systems it serves, with "alsoWhy" in plain words; the map draws it in both places (Destin, 2026-10-08: "why can we not tag as relevant to both?").

chat-view.purpose: The conversation itself: message bubbles, the scrolling timeline, find-in-chat and text formatting.

tool-cards.purpose: The little cards that show what the assistant did (ran a command, read a file, searched past chats).

chat-input.purpose: The box where you type and send a message, plus attachments, queued messages and the stop button.

attention-prompts.purpose: The banners and cards that stop and ask you something (pick an option, approve a plan, answer a question).

permission-prompts.purpose: The screens that ask "may the assistant do this?" and let you manage what it is allowed to do.

session-strip.purpose: The row of tabs along the top and the side drawer that list your open conversations.

session-resume.purpose: Picking an old conversation to reopen, and the choices offered when you do.

terminal-view.purpose: The raw terminal view of a conversation, for people who want to see what Claude Code shows.

status-bar.purpose: The strip showing the model, usage, cost and health of the current conversation.

model-picker.purpose: Choosing which AI model answers, and the prompts when you switch.

local-models-ui.purpose: Downloading and managing AI models that run on your own computer.

providers-ui.purpose: Signing in to AI providers (ChatGPT, OpenRouter, Claude) and showing which one is active.

specialists-ui.purpose: The helper assistants a conversation can hand work to, and their reports.

tags-ui.purpose: Labels and notes you attach to conversations to find them later.

buddy-ui.purpose: The small floating companion window that shows your assistant and its mascot.

voice-input.purpose: The microphone button that turns speech into a message.

chat-state.purpose: The behind-the-screen memory of a conversation: messages, sending, loading history, tasks.

skills-ui.purpose: Viewing, editing and running your installed skills from inside a chat.

transcript-pipeline.purpose: Reads Claude Code conversation files as they grow and turns them into messages on screen.

session-manager.purpose: Starts, tracks, names and closes the live conversations and their terminals.

claude-code-link.purpose: Connects YouCoded to Claude Code: its settings, hooks, built-in commands and prompts.

native-runtime.purpose: YouCoded own assistant engine: runs a conversation, keeps its history, assembles prompts.

native-permissions.purpose: Decides what the native assistant may do and remembers your approvals.

harness-tools.purpose: The abilities the native assistant can use: read and edit files, run commands, browse.

harness-injection.purpose: Extra information slipped into the assistant context before it answers.

harness-mcp.purpose: Lets the native assistant use outside tool servers (MCP).

harness-skills.purpose: Lets the native assistant find and use skills.

harness-search.purpose: Web search for the native assistant and where its search keys are kept.

harness-prompts.purpose: The standing instructions the native assistant is given.

harness-askpass.purpose: Safely asks you for an admin password when the assistant needs one.

native-specialists.purpose: Runs helper assistants on behalf of the main one.

providers.purpose: Sign-in and secret storage for cloud AI services, and the catalog of their models.

local-models.purpose: Downloads, sizes up and runs AI models on your own computer.

chatsearch-index.purpose: Builds the searchable index of all your past conversations.

conversation-store.purpose: Saves conversation titles, tags and records on disk.

voice-engine.purpose: Turns speech into text on your computer.

buddy-window.purpose: Opens and positions the floating companion window.

status-data.purpose: Collects the usage and health numbers shown in the status bar.

chat-contract.purpose: The agreed shapes of messages, sessions and prompts used by both sides of the app.

agent-contract.purpose: The agreed shapes for models, providers and the native assistant engine.

permissions-contract.purpose: The agreed shapes and rules for permissions, used by both sides.

pages-screens.purpose: Your Pages: small apps living inside YouCoded, their list, creation and display.

page-connections-ui.purpose: Choosing which outside accounts and data a Page may use.

page-runtime.purpose: Stores, serves and refreshes Pages and keeps their data.

page-connections.purpose: Holds the links between a Page and outside services.

pages-contract.purpose: The agreed shape of a Page and its tools.

marketplace-screens.purpose: Browsing, installing, liking and reviewing community skills and themes.

marketplace-state.purpose: Remembers what the marketplace screens have loaded and what you favorited.

marketplace-account-ui.purpose: Signing in to your community account.

marketplace-backend.purpose: Talks to the community server for listings, installs and sign-in.

marketplace-account.purpose: Your community account: sign-in tokens and profile.

theme-marketplace.purpose: Shares community themes and checks their submissions.

plugin-install.purpose: Installs and keeps up to date the add-ons that skills and themes ship in.

skill-library.purpose: Finds, shares and stores the skills installed on this computer.
skill-library.alsoWhy: Installed skills are what the assistant runs in chat; the library is where they live.

github-connection.purpose: Links your GitHub account so you can share your work.
github-connection.alsoWhy: The same GitHub sign-in publishes themes and plugins to the marketplace; 35% of its connections go there (edge audit 2026-10-08).

theme-share-ui.purpose: Sharing your own theme with the community.

marketplace-contract.purpose: The agreed shapes for community listings, skills and sign-in.

games-arcade.purpose: The built-in games, leaderboards and playing against friends.

social-presence.purpose: Shows which friends are around and lets you reach them.

project-view.purpose: The project screen: your files, folders and what the assistant changed.

artifact-views.purpose: Viewers and editors for documents, spreadsheets, code and images.

artifact-state.purpose: Tracks which files the assistant has made or changed.

document-comments-ui.purpose: Comments on documents shared between you and the assistant.

office-ui.purpose: Opening and editing Word, Excel and PowerPoint files inside the app.

git-review-ui.purpose: Reviewing the changes the assistant made to a project and undoing them.

artifacts.purpose: Finds and keeps track of the files a conversation produced.

document-comments.purpose: Reads and writes comments inside Word, Excel and other documents.

git-service.purpose: Reads the state of a project git history.

project-context.purpose: Understands a project: its folders, repository and instructions.

folders.purpose: Remembers the folders you work in.

file-access.purpose: Controls which files the app and your phone may read.

projects-contract.purpose: The agreed shapes for files, documents, folders and project history.

sync-spaces.purpose: Keeps your projects and conversations backed up and in step across your devices.

sync-service.purpose: The older sync and backup machinery and its error handling.

conversation-handoff.purpose: Moves a live conversation from one device to another.

remote-access.purpose: Lets your phone or a web browser use the app running on your computer.

device-identity.purpose: Gives each of your devices a name the others recognise.

sync-ui.purpose: Setting up and checking sync and backup.

remote-ui.purpose: Screens for connecting a phone or browser to this computer.

handoff-ui.purpose: The screens for moving a conversation between devices.

sync-contract.purpose: The agreed shapes used by sync and device pairing.

app-shell.purpose: The window itself: header, menus, startup, errors and layout on narrow screens.

settings-screens.purpose: The Settings window and its pages.

theming.purpose: Colors, wallpapers, fonts and effects that restyle the whole app.

ui-primitives.purpose: The shared buttons, dialogs, menus and inputs every screen is built from.

guide-tour.purpose: The tips and walkthrough that teach new people the app.

updates-ui.purpose: Checking for and installing app updates, and release notes.

performance-ui.purpose: The performance button and its options.

development-popups.purpose: Report a bug and contribute, from inside the app.

bridge-client.purpose: How screens talk to the rest of the app, on a computer or a phone.

renderer-utils.purpose: Small shared helpers for screens: time, sounds, announcements.

app-shell-backend.purpose: Starts the app, makes the windows, handles quitting and the operating system.

ipc-bridge.purpose: The one list of everything the screens can ask the app to do, and the code that answers.

theming-backend.purpose: Loads, watches and converts theme files.

updates.purpose: Downloads and installs new versions of the app.

app-telemetry.purpose: The daily anonymous check-in that says the app is in use.

first-run.purpose: Checks and installs what the app needs on first launch.

app-logging.purpose: Logs, crash reports and timing marks.

platform-support.purpose: Differences between Windows, Mac and Linux.

window-management.purpose: Opens, tracks and closes windows, including moving a chat into its own window.

shared-utils.purpose: Small helpers used everywhere: versions, time, text.

bridge-contract.purpose: The single list of requests between screens and the app, and their shapes.

app-contract.purpose: Shared shapes for updates, announcements, preferences and first-run.

workbench.purpose: The fake-backend playground where screens are built and previewed without the real app.

shoot-mode.purpose: The hooks that let the screenshot tool photograph named screens.

harness-eval.purpose: Scoring rig that compares how well different models drive the native assistant.

dev-probes.purpose: Small checks used when developing and launching the app.

android-app.purpose: The Android app built around the same screens.

android-runtime.purpose: Android version of the conversation runtime and terminal.

android-skills.purpose: Android version of skills and the marketplace.

android-bridge.purpose: Android connection between the screens and the phone code.

development-backend.purpose: Gathers what is needed to file a bug report or contribute a change, from inside the app.

unsorted-components.purpose: Loose screen pieces nobody has placed yet.

unsorted-state.purpose: Loose screen memory files nobody has placed yet.

unsorted-hooks.purpose: Loose screen helper files nobody has placed yet.
